Weeks 1-2: Foundation & Control

These first two weeks are about setting the standard for how you move, breathe, and control the weight. You’ll train around the 80% effort zone, focusing on clean reps, steady breathing, and strong positions. The goal isn’t to chase fatigue — it’s to build trust in your joints, posture, and technique while waking up muscle and nervous system coordination.

Think: smooth reps, controlled negatives, and learning how to create tension without fight. This phase sets the base that lets everything ramp up safely and effectively later.


Weeks 3-4: Strength, Density & Stability

Now that your movement patterns are locked in, we start increasing the density of work — slightly more volume, tighter rest, and stronger intent behind each rep. You’re still living in that 80% zone, but you’ll feel more muscular demand and deeper stability challenges.

This phase is about building muscle that works, not just muscle that looks good — better control through full ranges, stronger core integration, and smoother transitions between movements. Strength should feel more automatic and confident here.


Weeks 5-6: Performance & Output

In the final phase, you start turning that control into output and conditioning. Strength days stay controlled and intentional, but your full-body day becomes more athletic and demanding on your heart rate and recovery.

You’re learning how to switch gears — calm and precise when needed, aggressive and athletic when it’s time to push. This phase is where everything comes together: muscle, stamina, coordination, and confidence in your body’s ability to perform under stress without breaking down.
